name: Apparition for iOS
subtitle: The on-device sideloader
description: Official releases of Apparition. Every release is signed; see apparition.illixion.com.

apps.name: Apparition
apps.subtitle: Sideload, sign and refresh apps on the device itself
apps.localizedDescription: Install apps from AltStore-format sources, sign them on the device with a free Apple ID or your own certificate, keep them refreshed, and launch them with JIT.

versions.localizedDescription:
## New
- **Tools tab** in the device app, and the same tools from the command line (`processes`, `kill`, `location`, `logs`): running processes and ending an app, a simulated location, the device's console, activity and network monitors, connection conditions, developer service readiness, an app data browser with backups, and sysdiagnose.
- **Older devices:** Apparition now runs on iOS and tvOS 17.4 and visionOS 2, down from 26, and reaches iPhones on iOS 17.0–17.3 over the cable. This is best effort. An app newer than the device is refused before signing, and installs to iOS 16 and earlier from the desktop app are marked untested.
- **Apple TV away from home:** guidance for pairing at home and using a phone hotspot. Apparition stays running on the Apple TV while it is an app's JIT debugger.

## Improved
- A computer's pairing is healed when the device turns it down.
- The companion is found again when the device changes network, including over Tailscale.
- Mac apps are found over DebugTrace's local socket in the Store.
- The desktop app keeps its diagnostics in `apparition-core.log` with private values removed, and keeps its own build service reachable by skipping proxies on loopback.
- Install freshness is judged from the build's recorded sources, and a `-dirty` build says what made it so.
- Pairing keys no longer appear in the log.
- The macOS release files now build reproducibly.

**Apparition is now a development tool.** It supports several anisette sources, including its built-in Android provider, alongside a Mac you own.

**Mac, Windows or Linux**
- **The same app on all three.** Installing Apparition on a device, refreshing, JIT and the companion run the same on macOS, Windows (x64 and ARM64) and Linux (.deb and AppImage, x64 and ARM64), with no Mac involved. Only a free Apple ID's sign-in needs an anisette source. A Mac gives the most complete and most stable setup.
- **Setup for Windows (x64 and ARM64).** Apparition Setup puts the app in place and lets your devices through Windows' firewall, so you are never asked about it. Choose Only me, and the app keeps itself up to date without asking; or Everyone on this PC, which adds a background service (running with minimal rights, not as the system) that serves your devices with nobody signed in. The service follows the app's Settings, steps aside while the app is open and takes over again when it closes; pair devices in the app, since nobody is there to answer the service. Removing Apparition takes the rules and the service away with it. The zip is still there to unpack anywhere. Both need nothing Windows doesn't have: on a PC stripped of Edge's WebView2, the app says so and offers Microsoft's installer instead of failing to open.
- **A start-here guide for each computer** is in the README and on the website: how to get the app, pair an iPhone or iPad over USB (Apple Devices or iTunes on Windows, `usbmuxd` on Linux), and sign in.

**Signing in**
- **Your own Mac is the recommended source.** A Mac on macOS 26 or earlier gives its anisette with no setup and no change to its security, and your other Apple devices get the usual sign-in prompt. Windows and Linux computers, other Macs and your devices pair with it over an encrypted channel, with a six-digit code, and sign in through it.
- **macOS 27: a small VM.** macOS 27 keeps its anisette to itself, so on Apple silicon Apparition sets up a small macOS 26 virtual machine for it with one button, in the desktop app or with `apparition vm`. The catch: Apple sends a VM's sign-ins a code by SMS only, never a prompt on your devices.
- **Apparition's own Android anisette** works on macOS, Windows and Linux with no Mac at all: choose Apparition's own (Android libraries) when you sign in. It fetches Apple Music's Android libraries from Apple on first use and runs them in the app; where Apple's server can't be reached, it takes them from the Apple Music APK you choose, if it is the exact version Apparition was tested with (`apparition anisette import`, or Advanced under the sign-in error). It signs in on that computer, and the companion can offer it to your devices too (Settings > Anisette for your devices). Apple has closed this route and reopened it before, so a future update may switch it off. (Its most recent closure, in November, turned out to be a missing slash at the end of a URL: thanks to adriano6574, whose pull request found it.)
- **Run your own anisette server with Docker**, on Windows (Docker Desktop or WSL), Linux or macOS: `selfhost/anisette/compose.yaml` is back, pinned to a verified image. It is a sign-in with no Mac and no server from anyone else, with Apple's libraries kept out of Apparition's own process. Give Apparition `http://localhost:6970`.
- **Third-party anisette servers still work**, on every platform, with no Mac at all. Give a server's address in Settings and use Check server. Apparition doesn't supply one, and Apple decides what it accepts.
- **Connections refuse national interception CAs.** Every connection Apparition makes (sign-in, downloads, updates, anisette) checks certificates against your system's trust store, and refuses Russia's and Kazakhstan's national root CAs even where the system trusts them. App sources and IPA links are taken over https only.
- **Sign-ins send what Apple's own clients send.** Routing info and the request time now go in every sign-in request, whatever the anisette source; before, a plain server's sign-ins left them out.
- **A verbose record for when Apple changes something.** Settings > Troubleshooting on the device, Settings > Troubleshooting in the desktop app, `apparition --verbose` on the command line, or `setVerboseLog` for an agent writes each request a sign-in sends to Apple and the answer to `apparition-verbose.log`, as structure and sizes: no passwords, tokens or anisette values. Off unless you turn it on, and a file of its own, so it never ends up in the ordinary log.
- **Two-factor sign-in is sturdier.** It offers SMS when Apple answers with phone options, uses a code Apple has already texted, and keeps a sign-in log across launches.
- **Your device finds your computer by itself**, on your Wi-Fi at home and over Tailscale away, so the weekly refresh and JIT keep working wherever the device is.

**For developers**
- **Install apps or Develop apps.** The desktop app asks which on first run, and you can switch from its header at any time. Develop adds Apps, Debug and Builds tabs, a readiness checklist, and a pick-a-folder way to add an Xcode project.
- **The Apparition Store is built into the Mac app.** It builds and deploys your apps and keeps the builds, collects crash reports and DebugTrace traces, serves the debug console and an MCP server for agents, and needs nothing installed beside the app. It runs on Windows and Linux too.
- **Debug a running app.** Each running app has Tune, Log, Profile and Memory buttons. Values you tune become sliders, and crashes arrive symbolicated from the exact build on the device.
- **`apparition build`** builds with Xcode, signs, installs over Apparition's own pairing and launches, using Xcode's tunnel (`devicectl`) only as a fallback. It builds Mac apps too, and signs live-patch libraries.
- **`apparition launch`** starts an app with its console attached, and with JIT if you ask. **`apparition inject`** patches Swift into the running app, relaunching or attaching by itself when it has to.
- **Build from another computer.** Pair a Windows or Linux computer, or another Mac, with your Mac for developer access. Its builds go to your devices with `apparition deploy`, and its agents debug your apps through the Mac. Without a Mac, xtool builds on Linux (and Windows through WSL) and `apparition deploy` installs the result.
- **Also new:** an Updates view and `apparition updates` for keeping apps current, `apparition crash-reports` for reading what crashed, and `apparition container` to move an app's data off a device and back.

**When something goes wrong**
- **Report a Problem, on the device.** Settings > Report a Problem… makes a report of what the app was doing, with your Apple ID, team, device name and addresses left out. You read every file in it and remove what you like, and it is encrypted so only the maintainer can open it, even attached to a public issue. It then opens the bug form with the version, device and OS filled in.
- **On the desktop**, Settings > Troubleshooting > Report a problem… opens the desktop bug form with the version and your computer's OS filled in. It attaches nothing: the desktop app and the command line don't make an encrypted report yet, so describe the problem and don't attach log files to a public issue.
- **Separate forms** for the Apparition app, the desktop app and command line, and an app that won't install or run.
- **Debug your copy from your Mac.** Settings > Developer lets a Mac you pair reach the app's debug server for an hour, or until you turn it off. Off by default; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Installing and updating**
- **Updates close the app first.** Installing an update of a running app on a headset or phone closes it, as Xcode does, so the update applies at once instead of waiting for you to close the app. That covers installs from your Mac and from Apparition's own Library on the device.
- **Apparition updates itself the same way.** After a refresh you start, it asks "Close Apparition to finish updating?" and closes on your answer. A refresh the system starts closes it by itself when nobody is using it. Apparition never closes while an app is running under its JIT debugger.
- **`build-and-sign` and `apparition build` pick their route.** `--via auto` (the default) installs through Apparition's own pairing and falls back to Xcode's tunnel (`devicectl`) only when the device can't be reached that way. `--via devicectl` forces the tunnel, and `--via apparition` never falls back.
- **A dropped connection during an update is no longer a failure.** When the device holds an update until the app closes, the install is reported as queued.
- **The device finds your computer by name again** and lists it once, however many networks it hears it on. It also no longer saves the address of a virtual machine's bridge (the anisette VM's or Docker's), which it can never reach.

**Interface**
- Tabs and the setup steps ease in, and the header's three pills share one height.
- The header badge says where anisette comes from in one short line (`Anisette · VM`) with a status dot: green for a Mac's anisette, amber for Android or a server, red when sign-ins and the companion disagree, hollow when only this computer's sign-ins use it. Sign-ins and the companion use one anisette source.
- The desktop app's Settings can offer Apparition's own Android anisette to your devices, which suits a Mac with 8 GB that has no room for the anisette VM.

**Fixes**
- The desktop app's Settings no longer scrolls back to the top of an error every two seconds.
- A third-party anisette server that doesn't answer no longer hangs a sign-in, and one that answers without the headers Apple checks says so.
- Windows: the app's worker threads get 8 MiB of stack instead of Windows' 1 MiB, which a deep call could overflow (`0xc00000fd`), and so do the command line's. Reported by adriano6574.
- A failed write or close while sending an app to a device no longer panics; it reports where the upload stopped. Thanks to adriano6574.

- Desktop installers (macOS, Windows, Linux) can now update themselves. Updates are signed, checked only after you consent, and the tray has a new updates section. Checks now survive sleep and policy changes.
- Removing a library and approving JIT are more reliable.
- Each platform's app is bound to its signed IPA filename.
- A double-click no longer fires a control twice.
- Partial releases can now be built and selected by platform.
Apparition 0.4.4 (hotfix) fixes sign-in not working correctly in the Apple apps (visionOS, iOS and tvOS). The desktop installers are unchanged from 0.4.3, so this release only updates the apps.

**Sign-in works with the built-in anisette again.**
From 29 October, Apple's edge firewall rejected the legacy `Content-Type` that sideloaders send on every GrandSlam request. `gsd.apple.com` (provisioning) blocked `text/x-xml-plist`, and `gsa.apple.com` (sign-in) blocked `application/x-xml-plist`. It looked like Apple refusing Android anisette. Apparition now sends `text/xml`, which both accept, so a Mac's anisette, a third-party server or a macOS VM is no longer needed. They all still work if you prefer them. [Write-up](https://blog.illixion.com/2026/10/sideloading-error-80046/#update-30-october-it-was-the-content-type).

- **Hardware-identity fields in sign-in:** the request now carries `X-Mme-Legacy-Device-Id` and `X-Apple-I-MD-LU`, like Apple's own Windows client does.
- **Retry on another Apple server:** when one Apple server refuses a request or can't be reached, Apparition retries on another. Error messages are plainer and no longer suggest changing DNS.
- **Library matches appstore projects:** with the Mac build service connected, installed debuggable apps are grouped under their project. Cards show installed and retained builds, and offer an install review without rebuilding. They can also prepare newer builds automatically (you still approve installation), read symbolicated crash logs and trace files, and label iPhone and iPad compatibility-mode apps.
- **README and the macOS VM guide** no longer say a Mac's anisette is required.

**Sign-in works again.** Since October, Apple refuses the anisette Apparition's built-in provider makes on iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Vision Pro and Linux, and its GrandSlam servers were returning intermittent 503s on top of that.

- **Retries transient GrandSlam 503s** at the start of sign-in, at the password proof, and when asking for the Xcode token, so one bad answer no longer fails the whole sign-in.
- **Anisette from a macOS VM.** A VM's sign-in is accepted when the server forwards the host's attestation headers and claims the VM's real identity. `apparition anisette serve` does this inside a logged-in macOS session.
- **[Guide](https://github.com/illixion/Apparition/blob/main/docs/ANISETTE_VM.md) and one-line setup script** for turning a UTM macOS VM into that server: run `bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://apparition.illixion.com/avm.sh)"` in recoveryOS.
- **README:** the sign-in requirement is now a prominent alert. It lays out two paths: a third-party anisette server (quick, but could stop working) or your own macOS VM (reliable, about 20 minutes to set up).
- **Developer tab (new, inert until you connect a Mac build service):** Apparition desktop and the device can connect to a Mac running the build service to browse builds, register Xcode projects and install retained builds. The `apparition xcode` command registers existing Xcode products.
- **Vision Pro live-patching validation** work for development builds.

## Fixes

- **JIT for apps inside LiveContainer (#15).** With LiveContainer's JIT enabler set to StikDebug, Launch with JIT now works. A JIT link that names no process now launches the app again under the debugger, as StikDebug does, so LiveContainer starts the app you chose with JIT. Before, Apparition attached to the copy of LiveContainer waiting for it, and the app never got JIT.
- **Stop always ends a JIT session,** including while it is still starting. Before, it did nothing until the debugger had attached.

## New

- **StikDebug JIT scripts.** A script sent with the JIT request (as LiveContainer sends one you added to an app) now runs as the app's debugger. Apparition asks you first every time, because a script can read and change everything in the app.
- **JITProbe**, a minimal test app in the repository: it asks for JIT memory, writes code into it and runs it, and says "JIT works".

Tested on an iPhone 15 Pro Max with iOS 27.0.1 and LiveContainer Nightly, with and without StikDebug's `universal.js`.

## Dependency changes

- **zip 9.1.** Apparition now reads IPAs and `.deb` packages with zip 9.1, which fixes a parsing difference between an archive's two headers (GHSA-m665-v7pm-7grj). That only matters to software that checks an archive with one of the library's readers and extracts it with the other. Apparition uses a single reader for both, so it wasn't affected. Entries whose names can't be decoded are now skipped rather than guessed at.

## Fixes

- **Sign-in "403 Forbidden" (#12).** Some of Apple's `gsd.apple.com` servers refuse sign-in from some networks, depending on your DNS resolver. Apparition now avoids a server that does this for an hour and retries on another one, found through your system DNS or DNS-over-HTTPS. A connection that fails or times out gets one retry on other servers. If every server refuses, the error says Apple turned the network away and what to try.
- **Sign-in status is visible.** The status and its Try again button now appear under the form, and an error scrolls into view, instead of sitting below the fold.
- **Stale Library errors.** Cards now say when the last failure happened ("Failed 2 days ago"), and failures that blame an anisette address are dropped once that address changes.

## New

- **Anisette libraries from a file.** When Apple's download server can't be reached, the desktop app offers Try again and, under Advanced, using Apple Music's libraries from a file. `apparition anisette import` does the same from the command line. Files are checked against the tested version, and a mismatch can be overridden, which is flagged as an unsupported setup. The troubleshooting steps are in the README.
- **Setup badge.** The desktop header always shows where sign-in anisette comes from and what the companion offers.
- **App ID management and reuse.** The desktop app lists your App IDs with quota, expiry, search and deletion. The desktop and native iPhone, iPad, Vision Pro and Apple TV installers share extension selection and App ID reuse. Assignments are saved per team, device and source app, so one registered App ID can serve different apps on different devices.
- **Linux.** Flatpak bundles and direct package downloads.

Windows and the Linux GUI were tested only partly (unit tests and builds). The new sign-in and error handling is covered by unit tests on macOS and Windows.

* Connection: choose Companion or Local VPN, each with its own anisette server. iPhone and iPad can use LocalDevVPN without a computer.
* LiveContainer: export your signing certificate as a .p12 (Settings > Share Signing) for LiveContainer's JIT-less mode. Tested with Delta on iOS 27; see Supported apps.
* Stop: a new Stop button ends a refresh or install at any step.
* Clearer failures: an unreachable anisette server or device says so and offers to retry or switch modes, and a refresh no longer retries a sign-in that already failed.
* Security: rustls is updated for four advisories, and the trusted root CAs drop eMudhra's emSign roots. TLS is what protects the anisette library Apparition downloads.
* Privacy: the Apple ID, team, certificate names, URLs and addresses are kept out of the logs.
* Fixes: a just-installed app is no longer reported missing, Remove from Library works for apps deleted from the Home Screen, and the Share Signing share sheet stays open.

Command line ships inside the Mac app, with apparition link. Choose the signer at install time; data moves when an app changes team. Pairing fails fast, with pairing hand-off, and the device says why it can't be reached.

Apps published as a `.deb` package, such as Kodi, now install. Apparition unpacks the app from the package, so Kodi's official download works as it is. On a Vision Pro, iPhone or iPad, download the `.ipa` or `.deb` in Safari and share it to Apparition, or open it from Files, or use Library > Install from a File: Apparition names the app and asks before installing it. The desktop app (Advanced, An app file) and `apparition install` take a `.deb` too, and a source can list one.

Signing no longer fails on apps that carry object files, which Kodi's bundled Python does (`__LINKEDIT isn't final Mach-O segment`, #7).

A key arriving from another device keeps your Apple ID session, and sign-ins that can't be answered no longer prompt for 2FA. iPhone and iPad build from the main Apparition scheme. The desktop app's window buttons on macOS now line up with the header.
Fixes the Enable JIT prompt on Apple Vision Pro: it opens in its own window in front of you instead of a popover that could land out of reach. Apps only; the desktop installers stay at 0.3.0.

Signing in with the built-in anisette works again. Since 22 October Apple refuses the developer token (-80046) to sign-ins that claim to be an Android phone, which the built-in anisette has to claim, so Apparition now claims a Mac for that one request. Apparition also claims whatever each anisette server reports, so servers that don't run Apple's Android libraries work too.

Your devices now share one certificate instead of making one each. Signing stops before it would make a second Apparition certificate and offers to get the key from the device that has it, nearby over the local network, checked by a six-digit code both screens show: Settings > Get Signing from Another Device and Share Signing with Another Device, Apple TV included. The desktop app and `apparition signing send` and `signing receive` do the same. When the account has no certificate left, Apparition offers this before revoking one, and `apparition signing hand-off` gives the computer's key to an Apparition installed another way.

On Apple TV, free accounts now get a tvOS profile instead of error 8220, Apparition has a home screen icon, and Refresh All is at the top of the Library. Signing refuses an app built for other devices before it uses up one of the week's ten App IDs, and says which version to look for. Adding a source again takes its new options.

Thanks to valentinBoch for the tvOS profile, icon, anisette and isideload 0.5.0 work (#1, #3, #4, #5, #6).

Apparition can now be Madeira's JIT debugger. It answers the links Madeira opens, serves the game for its whole run, and can attach to an app that is already running. While it debugs, Apparition keeps running in the background (silent audio on visionOS, coarse location on iOS) and shows "Debugging Madeira" beside the tabs and in a notification, each with a Stop button. Apps that ask for the increased memory limit get it, along with extended virtual addressing on paid teams.

A new install is now waited for until it finishes; only an update to an app that's open is left queued.

On the command line, `apparition jit` starts or attaches a JIT session and `apparition sign` signs for a paired device without reaching it.

Add sources from a link: an "Add to Apparition" button on a source's page (apparition://source?url=…) opens Add Source with it filled in, ready to add. The desktop app's pairing steps now cover Apple TV too, including the second code it shows for Apparition.

First release. Sideload, sign and refresh apps on the device itself, on Apple Vision Pro, iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, with a free Apple ID (working again after Apple's 12 October change) or your own certificate. The desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux installs it and can stay on as its companion.
